Who runs n8n Developers

We're an automation team, not a tool reseller

n8n Developers is a forward-deployed automation studio built under Labs 24. We embed with teams, find the manual work, and stay on the hook for it after launch. That's the whole model.

Why we exist

Automation tools are easy to buy. Automation that actually ships is not.

n8n is powerful, flexible infrastructure, and most businesses don't have an engineer who can turn that flexibility into a working system, or the time to maintain one once it's live. We're the team that does both: we build the workflow and we own what happens to it in production.

What we believe about automation

Deployment isn't the finish line

A workflow going live is the start of the engagement, not the end of it. Systems change, edge cases appear, and someone has to stay responsible for that.

Use whatever the outcome requires

n8n is our orchestration layer, not a religion. AI models, APIs, custom code and databases all get used when the business outcome actually needs them.

A human checks what matters

AI steps get used where they're genuinely reliable, with approval gates and escalation paths everywhere the cost of a mistake is high, patient data, money, legal documents.

How we work

A small, forward-deployed team, not a help desk

Every engagement gets an automation engineer who sits with your team and stays accountable for the result, pulling in a specialist when a build needs one.

1

We start with one process, not a platform rollout

No multi-month discovery phase before anything ships. We find one real, repetitive process and prove the approach on it first.

2

We build with the right tools for the job

Custom code, APIs and databases get used wherever n8n's native nodes don't reach. The goal is a working system, not a pure-n8n showcase.

3

We stay on after launch

Monitoring, error handling and a weekly backlog review are part of every engagement, not a separate support contract you have to negotiate later.

Comparison

Forward deployed engineer vs agency vs freelancer: which should you hire?

Which suits your process: a freelancer, an agency or an embedded engineer?

Book a callLearn more about FDE

Where does each option fit?

Freelancer

Fits when

  • You have one well-defined workflow
  • You can write the brief and review the work
  • You want a short, flexible engagement

Falls short when

  • Nobody else knows how it was built
  • There is no cover when they are away
  • Nobody watches runs after delivery

Automation agency

Fits when

  • You have a larger project with a clear scope
  • You want a team and a project manager
  • You have a plan to hand over at launch

Falls short when

  • Work is handed over and nobody owns upkeep
  • The team learns your process from documents
  • Changes after launch need a new scope

Forward deployed engineer

Fits when

  • You have several connected processes
  • The process is messy or undocumented
  • You want someone accountable after launch

Falls short when

  • You have a single one-off task
  • You only want advice and no build
  • You prefer to run everything yourself

How do they compare side by side?

FreelancerAgencyForward deployed engineer
Where they workRemotely, on a taskIn their own team, on a projectInside your process, with your team
How they learn your processFrom your briefFrom discovery documents and callsBy working alongside the people who do it

How do you choose between them?

  1. Count the processes

    One well-defined workflow can suit a freelancer. Several connected processes suit an embedded engineer.

  2. Ask who will maintain it

    If nobody on your team can look after the automation, you need someone accountable after launch.

  3. Weigh the cost of a silent failure

    If a failed run costs you money or customers, choose a team that monitors, not only builds.

  4. Start with one process

    Bring one real process to a call. We will say honestly whether it needs a freelancer, an agency or us.

How does an n8n Developers forward deployed engineer work?

An n8n Developers forward deployed engineer joins your process, learns how the work really runs, builds the automation on n8n and AI, and stays accountable after launch. We also say plainly when another option fits you better.

Learn more about FDE

Questions about forward deployed engineer vs agency vs freelancer

What is the difference between a forward deployed engineer and an agency?

An agency usually delivers a defined project and hands it over. A forward deployed engineer works inside your process, builds the solution, and stays accountable after launch.

When is a freelancer enough?

When you have one well-defined workflow, can write a clear brief, and can review and maintain the result yourself. A freelancer is also a good fit for a short, one-off job.

Can I start with a freelancer and move to a forward deployed engineer later?

Yes. Many teams start small. If workflows multiply or something breaks and nobody owns it, an embedded engineer can document what exists, fix what is fragile and take over monitoring.

How much does each option cost?

It depends on the scope, the tools involved and how much ongoing support you want. Contact us with one process and we will scope it on a call and give you a clear answer.

Is a frontend deployed engineer the same as a forward deployed engineer?

Usually yes. It is a common variant spelling of forward deployed engineer, which is the standard term.

What is a forward deployed engineer, in plain words?

Think of it as a specialist who moves in for the project. Instead of writing requirements and waiting for a vendor, you get someone sitting next to your team who sees the problem first-hand.

  2. Your tools do not talk to each other

    People copy data between systems, so mistakes creep in.

How do you choose between them?

  1. List the process steps

    Write the steps the process follows, including the exceptions.

  2. Check for custom logic or AI

    If a step needs custom rules, code or AI, lean toward n8n. If it is simple app-to-app, Zapier or Make may be enough.

  3. Decide who maintains it

    The platform you can keep running matters more than the one with the longest feature list.

  4. Ask for a second opinion

    A forward deployed engineer can review the process and recommend a platform, including when it is not n8n.

An n8n Developers forward deployed engineer joins your process, learns how the work really runs, builds the automation on n8n and AI, and stays accountable after launch. We also say plainly when another option fits you better.

How is n8n different from Zapier or Make?

n8n suits workflows that need custom logic, AI steps or control over where data lives, and it can be self-hosted. Zapier and Make are simpler to start with. We can advise on which fits your process.

Is n8n free, and is self-hosting cheaper than n8n Cloud?

n8n can be self-hosted under its Sustainable Use License, and its terms differ for some commercial uses, so check which applies to you. Self-hosting also adds maintenance work, so it is not always cheaper overall.

Yes. We list what you run today, rebuild the automations in n8n one at a time, run old and new side by side, and switch each over only after it matches.

Do I need a developer to use n8n?

Not always. Simple workflows can be built by non-technical staff. Complex logic, AI steps and self-hosting are easier with an engineer, which is where a forward deployed engineer helps.

What does a forward deployed engineer do for a SaaS team?

A forward deployed engineer is an engineer who works inside your business instead of from a distance. For a SaaS team the engineer connects the product, CRM and support tool, so new customers get the right next step and customer success hears about stalled accounts early.

Step by step

How do you automate SaaS customer onboarding step by step?

  1. Define activation

  2. Connect signup and usage events

  3. Branch by plan and behavior

    Send different messages depending on plan and on what the customer has or has not done yet.

  4. Alert customer success on stalls
